sections.h2: Where does a Vinton County deed get recorded?
sections.html:
At the courthouse in McArthur, 100 East Main Street, OH 45651. The recorder answers at 740-596-4314 from 8:30 am to 4:00 pm on weekdays, according to the county's directory of offices.

Besides deeds and mortgages, the counter takes oil and gas leases, military discharge papers, and tax, unemployment and workers compensation liens. Staff help where they can, yet they do not run searches, assist with wording or sell blank forms. Anyone who needs a deed written should line up a title company or lawyer before the trip.

sections.h2: What is it like to sell a house in Vinton County?
sections.html:
Vinton County lies in the Hocking Hills region of southeastern Ohio. It was carved out in 1850 from parts of Ross, Gallia, Jackson, Hocking and Athens counties, spans 414 square miles and has about 13,000 people. McArthur, the seat since 1815, sits at the crossing of State Route 93 and U.S. 50.

The county has no cities and, by its own account, only one traffic light. Four villages hold the population centers: McArthur (1,701 in the 2010 census), Hamden (879), Zaleski (278) and Wilkesville (149). Twelve townships cover the rest of the map: Brown, Clinton, Eagle, Elk, Harrison, Jackson, Knox, Madison, Richland, Swan, Vinton and Wilkesville. Over eighty percent of the land is wooded, and state parks, forests and part of the Wayne National Forest bring in hikers, boaters and hunters.

The school district runs Vinton County High School on U.S. 50 and the middle school on Locker Plant Road, both in McArthur, with elementary schools in Hamden (South) and Allensville (West). The county's utility list names the McArthur Water Department and several water companies, along with AEP, Buckeye Rural Electric and Columbia Gas. For owners fixing up a house before a sale, the Development Department at 740-596-3529 says income-eligible residents can ask about loans or grants for emergency repairs, septic systems or potable water.

sections.h2: How do you look up a recorded deed in Vinton County?
sections.html:
The office holds deed books and indexes from 1850 through December 31, 1985. From January 1, 1986 on, the index is searchable on the county's Ava site, with names and index data but no images.

For new filings the recorder's page says the office is fully online for transfer documents and lists ePN (888-325-3365) and CSC (866-652-0111) as e-recording routes. Property owners can also enroll in a free fraud alert at propertyfraudalert.com or 1-800-728-3858, which pings them when something is filed against their parcel.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record in Vinton County?
sections.html:
Ohio's section 317.32 sets the base amounts: $17 plus a matching $17 trust fund fee for the first two pages, and $4 plus $4 for each page after. A county can tack on a preservation surcharge capped at $5. The Vinton County recorder has posted a revised fee schedule and guidelines effective January 1, 2025 through the Ohio Recorders Association, so confirm the total with the office before sending a check.

  • Zoning resolutions: $25 plus $25.
  • Zoning amendments: $10 plus $10.
  • A certified copy: $1 plus $1 per page, and the seal costs 50 cents plus 50 cents.

sections.h2: Which Vinton County offices does a sale touch?
sections.html:
Every office a seller needs sits at the same address, so one morning can cover a long list. The table uses the numbers printed on county pages.

Vinton County courthouse offices in a home sale (county directory and auditor and treasurer pages)
OfficeRole in a salePhone
EngineerApproves deed and land contract descriptions, keeps tax maps740-790-7014
AuditorStatement of value, conveyance fee, transfers on the tax list740-790-7007
RecorderRecords the deed or mortgage740-596-4314
TreasurerCollects property tax, confirms what is owed740-790-7045
Clerk of CourtsCourt filings, titles and passports740-596-3001

The county engineer, according to the county's directory, approves every deed and land contract description. Splitting a rural tract is common in this county, so that stop comes first, and the auditor's endorsement comes before the recorder will accept the deed.

sections.h2: What does the Vinton County auditor charge on a sale?
sections.html:
The auditor's conveyance fee page states one figure: $4.00 per thousand dollars of the sale price, on real estate and manufactured homes alike. The grantor pays it when the deed is presented. State law, in 319.54 and 322.02, allows a $1 per $1,000 fee plus an optional county tax of up to thirty cents per hundred dollars.

The same office keeps the valuation side of the file. Its triennial update page explains that state law expects values to land between 90 and 110 percent of market, measured against sales from the preceding three years, and the letter on that page warned owners to expect a notable jump in value after the last update. The Board of Revision, with the auditor as secretary alongside the treasurer and the commissioners' president, takes value complaints that reach the auditor by March 31 each year.

The homestead page describes a credit that shields up to $26,200 of market value from local taxes for qualifying seniors and permanently disabled owners, and for 2025 payable in 2026 it required new applicants to have adjusted income under $40,000.

sections.h2: Which Vinton County transfers owe no conveyance fee?
sections.html:
The statute carves out many cases, and a filing in one of them gives the reason instead of a price. Examples a Vinton County family might meet:

  • A gift between spouses or from a parent to a child.
  • A deed that fixes an error in an earlier recorded deed.
  • A trust deed the maker can revoke.
  • Property split among heirs for no payment.
  • A transfer to a nonprofit charity without payment.
  • An easement valued at $1,000 or less.

sections.h2: How are Vinton County property taxes handled around a closing?
sections.html:
The treasurer's page warns of a 5 percent penalty on second-half bills left unpaid past the closing date and 10 percent ten days after, citing ORC 323.121. Second-half 2026 real estate and manufactured home tax was due July 30. Payment can be made by check, money order, cash or card (the card carries a 2.75 percent fee), and a drop box sits in the alley behind the courthouse, where the page asks people not to leave cash.

The 2026 rate sheet for tax year 2025 divides the county into 18 taxing districts. Its residential and agricultural column shows 34.280207 for Brown-Vinton, 43.440994 for the Hamden corporation, 43.551322 for Zaleski and 48.162418 for the McArthur corporation, expressed per thousand dollars of valuation. Village parcels carry a higher total than township parcels.

If a bill has not arrived, call the treasurer at 740-790-7045, because a title company needs the true balance before closing.

faqs.q: What is the phone number for the Vinton County recorder?
faqs.a: The number is 740-596-4314. The office is at 100 East Main Street in McArthur and is open weekdays from 8:30 am to 4:00 pm.

faqs.q: Can a deed be e-recorded in Vinton County?
faqs.a: Yes. The recorder says it accepts transfer documents electronically and names ePN and CSC as e-recording partners. Paper still goes to the courthouse counter.

faqs.q: How much is the Vinton County conveyance fee?
faqs.a: The auditor's page says $4.00 per thousand dollars of the sale price. It applies to real estate and manufactured home sales, and the seller pays it at the auditor's office before the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Will the Vinton County recorder help draft a deed?
faqs.a: No. The recorder's page says staff do not search records, help prepare a document or provide recording forms. A title company or attorney should handle the drafting.

faqs.q: How do I get an alert if a document is filed on my Vinton County property?
faqs.a: Sign up for the free property fraud alert at propertyfraudalert.com or by calling 1-800-728-3858. The county recorder offers it through its recording service provider.
